tour.windowTitle: How to use the Media tab

intro.title: The Media studio
intro.body: Generate images, video, music, speech (TTS) and transcripts (STT) from one place. Runs free on your machine — no key, no credits — or connect Surplus, Venice, or imgnAI for cloud models, each with its own catalog. Pick the provider at the top. Two sub-tabs up here: Generate (this one) and Artifacts (your saved library).

importUrl.title: Import from a URL
importUrl.body: Paste a link from YouTube, Instagram, X, or 1000+ other sites to pull a file straight into your media library — then remix it or use it as a reference image or video.

modality.title: Pick a modality
modality.body: Choose what to create — the model list and controls adapt to it. Local covers image, video and speech (TTS) with models you download once and run for free; Surplus and Venice add music and transcripts (STT) plus their own cloud catalogs, and imgnAI adds another image/video catalog.

localEngine.title: The local engine
localEngine.body: Download an open model here once — sizes are shown up front — then generate fully offline for free, with speed packs available to cut steps on supported models.

model.title: Pick a model
model.body: Each modality + provider lists its own models, and the controls change per model — sizes, voices, durations, aspect ratios appear only when that model supports them.

prompt.title: Prompt + reference image
prompt.body: Describe what you want and tune the per-model params. Models that support it show a "Reference image" control — for img2img / image EDITING, or as the first frame for image-to-video.

generate.title: Generate
generate.body: Hit Generate. Local runs right here — no key, no credits, first run just downloads the model once. Image/TTS/STT are instant; video/music run async with a progress readout. Cloud providers need their own key: a funded Surplus key, a Venice key, or an imgnAI key.

gallery.title: Your gallery + Artifacts
gallery.body: Every result is saved here and survives restart — Save to a folder, Reveal on disk, Remix to reload its settings, or open fullscreen. The Artifacts sub-tab is the full library of everything you have made.

workflow.title: Tip: build it as a node workflow
workflow.body: Open the Nodes tab to chain it: a Prompt node writes the prompt, a Reference-Image node feeds a character, a Media node generates — and each run drops a result card you can branch from. Or open the Storyboard starter template to chain a local still into two local video scenes end to end.

negative_prompt.label: Negative prompt
negative_prompt.description: What to avoid (artifacts, watermarks, extra limbs, …).

n.label: Images
n.description: How many images to generate in one run. The checkpoint loads once, but each image is sampled in full — 4 images take about 4x as long as 1. Each gets its own seed, counting up from the first.

seed.label: Seed
seed.description: -1 = random. Lock a value to reproduce a result.

cfg.label: Guidance (CFG)
cfg.description: How strictly to follow the prompt.

strength.label: img2img strength
strength.description: Only with an init image. 0 = keep init, 1 = ignore it.

language.label: Language
language.description: ISO code hint (e.g. "en"). Leave blank to auto-detect.

clip_skip.label: CLIP skip
clip_skip.description: How many of the text encoder's last layers to ignore. 0 leaves it to the engine (1 for SD 1.x). Many Civitai SD 1.5 merges — anime ones especially — were trained at 2 and look flat and washed out at 1; if a checkpoint's own page names a CLIP skip, this is where it goes.

vae_tiling.label: Tile the VAE decode
vae_tiling.description: Decode the picture in tiles instead of all at once. This is the flag that turns an out-of-memory death in the final decode into a finished render — on video it is the step that actually gets killed. Costs a little time and can leave faint seams between tiles.

vae_conv_direct.label: Direct VAE convolutions
vae_conv_direct.description: Use the direct convolution path in the autoencoder. Lower peak memory in the decode for the same maths — try it before tiling, since it has no seams to trade.

max_vram.label: VRAM budget
max_vram.description: Split each forward pass so the model does not have to fit in video memory at once — the engine's own answer to a model that is bigger than the card. "auto" uses the free VRAM the driver reports, keeping 1 GiB spare; a number is a hard budget in GiB. Off means no splitting, which is what every run has done until now.

stream_layers.label: Stream layers
stream_layers.description: Keep only the layers in use resident and prefetch the next ones — the rung after the budget on upstream's own ladder. It needs a VRAM budget set above, and it needs the model's weights held in RAM, which this turns on for you. Auto-fit below takes that placement back, so the two cannot both be on: with auto-fit the engine decides, and this is left off.

auto_fit.label: Auto-fit to this machine
auto_fit.description: Let the engine place the diffusion model, the text encoder and the autoencoder itself, from the model's size and the memory each device has free. It replaces the app's own placement (including keeping the text encoders on the CPU) and may split the model across more than one GPU.
